claims.text: Đơn Hàng's database is run by the PostgreSQL program; db/seed.sql fills it; its first orders row is ( 1, 1, '2026-03-02 09:15:00+07', 'paid') (id, customer_id, placed_at, status: no name, no product); products come first (lines 5-13) and each order_items row holds four numbers.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang@stage-0: db/seed.sql lines 23-24, 37-49; db/schema.sql lines 18-32; STAGE.md (db created from schema.sql and seed.sql)

claims.text: A primary key's values must be both unique and not null, so PostgreSQL rejects a row whose key has no value (NULL) or repeats the key of a row already in the table; a primary key can span more than one column.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §5.5.4 Primary Keys

claims.text: Keep a primary key value unchanged once assigned, because other rows store it to point at the row; with foreign keys written like Đơn Hàng's (no ON UPDATE, so NO ACTION, claim 18) PostgreSQL refuses the change only while a referencing row exists.
claims.source_hint: Outline item 1; PostgreSQL 17 docs §5.5.5 Foreign Keys (referencing rows hold the referenced value)

claims.text: A foreign key requires the column's value, when not NULL, to match the referenced column (a primary key or unique column; in Đơn Hàng always the primary key) in some row of the table it points at: PostgreSQL refuses an orders row whose customer_id matches no customers.id.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §5.5.5 Foreign Keys; db/schema.sql@stage-0 line 20

claims.text: A one-to-many relationship is stored as a foreign key on the many side: orders.customer_id (NOT NULL) gives each order exactly one customer, and nothing limits how many orders share one customer.
claims.source_hint: db/schema.sql@stage-0 lines 18-24; PostgreSQL 17 docs §5.5.5 Foreign Keys

claims.text: A single-value foreign key column in orders could point at only one product, and one in products at only one order; a many-to-many relationship uses a separate table with a foreign key to each side, as order_items does.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §5.5.5 ("used to implement many-to-many relationships", products/orders/order_items example); db/schema.sql@stage-0 lines 26-32

claims.text: Normalisation means arranging tables so each fact is stored once; in Đơn Hàng the customer's name exists only as customers.full_name, and orders has no name column.
claims.source_hint: Outline item 4; db/schema.sql@stage-0 lines 11-24

claims.text: db/schema.sql at stage-0 creates six tables: products, customers, orders, order_items, payments, notifications; the diagram shows four of them and some columns; its end marks (|| exactly one, o{ zero or more) restate each line's label.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang db/schema.sql@stage-0 (six CREATE TABLE statements); Mermaid erDiagram relationship cardinality syntax

claims.text: In CREATE TABLE, each column definition gives the column name, its data type, then optional constraints such as PRIMARY KEY, NOT NULL, UNIQUE, CHECK and REFERENCES, which every row must satisfy; a definition may continue on the next line (status's CHECK).
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs SQL Commands: CREATE TABLE (column_constraint); §5.1 Table Basics; §5.5 Constraints

claims.text: GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY makes id an identity column: when an inserted row gives no value, PostgreSQL assigns the next value from the column's implicit sequence; a value given explicitly is accepted.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §5.3 Identity Columns; CREATE TABLE GENERATED { ALWAYS | BY DEFAULT } AS IDENTITY

claims.text: A UNIQUE constraint on email makes PostgreSQL refuse a second customers row with the same email value; email is not the table's primary key.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §5.5.3 Unique Constraints; db/schema.sql@stage-0 lines 11-16

claims.text: REFERENCES customers (id) on customer_id declares the foreign key, and NOT NULL on the same column means no orders row can exist without a customer.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §5.5.2 Not-Null Constraints, §5.5.5 Foreign Keys (column constraint form); db/schema.sql@stage-0 line 20

claims.text: PRIMARY KEY (order_id, product_id), a table constraint line and not a column, declares a primary key over two columns, so each (order, product) pair appears at most once in order_items; two units of one product are one row with quantity 2.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §5.5.4 Primary Keys (table constraint over a group of columns); db/schema.sql@stage-0 lines 26-32

claims.text: The seed row ( 1, 2, 2,  450000) in order_items is order 1, product 2, quantity 2, unit_price_vnd 450000, in whole đồng.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang db/seed.sql@stage-0 line 38; db/schema.sql lines 1-2 (money in whole đồng)

claims.text: order_items has its own unit_price_vnd column, separate from products.price_vnd; its name (price per unit) is what gives it the job of the price charged. Payment 1 (2150000) equals order 1's sum of quantity × unit_price_vnd.
claims.source_hint: db/schema.sql@stage-0 lines 4-8, 26-32; db/seed.sql lines 38, 52 (1250000 + 2 × 450000 = 2150000)

claims.text: When a product's price can change later, store the price charged on the order item, because old orders must keep what they cost; this does not store one fact twice.
claims.source_hint: Outline item 4 (each fact once); db/schema.sql@stage-0 order_items.unit_price_vnd

claims.text: Copying a fact into several tables on purpose for speed is a real technique, usually kept for a slowdown that has been measured, and whoever does it must keep every copy in step.
claims.source_hint: Outline misconception 1; opposing view required by prompt 00 for contested topics

claims.text: With REFERENCES and no ON UPDATE/ON DELETE clause the action is NO ACTION: PostgreSQL raises an error when a referenced key value is updated or its row deleted while referencing rows still exist.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §5.5.5 Foreign Keys (NO ACTION is the default; ON UPDATE analogous to ON DELETE); db/schema.sql@stage-0

claims.text: Do not use a meaningful value such as a phone number or email as a primary key when it can change or be shared (people change numbers and addresses, a family may share a phone); use a generated counter as Đơn Hàng does, and keep such values UNIQUE if needed.
claims.source_hint: Outline misconception 2; db/schema.sql@stage-0 customers (identity id, email UNIQUE)

claims.text: payments and notifications each have their own id primary key and an order_id column with REFERENCES orders (id) and no UNIQUE constraint, so one order can have many of each and each belongs to one order.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang db/schema.sql@stage-0 lines 34-48

claims.text: In SQL, two dashes (--) start a comment that runs to the end of the line; PostgreSQL removes it before analysing the statement, so the line -- lesson: … in db/schema.sql has no effect on the tables.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §4.1.5 Comments; db/schema.sql@stage-0 line 10

claims.text: In PostgreSQL 17, integer holds whole numbers, text holds character strings, and timestamptz is the alias of timestamp with time zone, a type that records a moment in time.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs Chapter 8 Data Types (Table 8.1 aliases; §8.1 Numeric, §8.3 Character, §8.5 Date/Time Types)

claims.text: Đơn Hàng's database is created from two files: PostgreSQL carries out db/schema.sql (makes the six tables) and then db/seed.sql (fills them).
claims.source_hint: don-hang@stage-0: STAGE.md line 18 (created from db/schema.sql and db/seed.sql); docker-compose.yml lines 67-68 (10-schema.sql, 20-seed.sql in /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d)

beyond_scope: Section 5 names GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY, UNIQUE, NOT NULL, CHECK, the -- comment and three data types (integer, text, timestamptz) in one clause each, because the quoted CREATE TABLE lines cannot be read without them; no SQL beyond the schema file is taught.
Section 5 notes that unit_price_vnd is a separate fact from products.price_vnd, so the quoted schema does not look like it breaks outline item 4.
